(a) In General.—Not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall establish a pilot program to assess the viability of commercial satellite weather data to support requirements of the Department of Defense. 
    (b) Duration.—The Secretary may carry out the pilot program under subsection (a) for a period not exceeding one year. 
    (c) Briefings.—
        (1) Interim briefing.—Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate (and to any other congressional defense committee upon request) demonstrating how the Secretary plans to implement the pilot program under subsection (a). 
        (2) Final briefing.—Not later than 90 days after the pilot program under subsection (a) is completed, the Secretary shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate (and to any other congressional defense committee upon request) on the utility, cost, and other considerations regarding the purchase of commercial satellite weather data to support the requirements of the Department of Defense.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the briefings, or the reference to "commercial" satellite weather data, bring outside parties into a federal decision. The briefings go only to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. The pilot program concerns assessing and buying commercial data, which is procurement, not consultation with companies or the public before a decision. The section sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to provide briefings to congressional committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not constitute participation by outside parties. There is no mention of consulting with the public, states, tribes, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate

opus.w: The only process this section requires is briefings to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. Testing commercial satellite weather data makes the providers sellers, not participants. The section has no requirement to consult them, no advisory panel, no hearing, no comment period, no rulemaking and no right to sue, so no outside party takes part in the Defense Department's decision.
opus.s: the Secretary shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate (and to any other congressional defense committee upon request) on the utility, cost, and other considerations regarding the purchase of commercial satellite weather data
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "commercial satellite weather data" brings private companies into a Defense Department decision. It doesn't. The pilot only tests whether the Department can use data bought from commercial providers, which makes those providers vendors, not participants. The only formal interaction required is briefings to the Armed Services Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Defense to provide briefings to congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Therefore, this interaction is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation with parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary of Defense shall provide a briefing to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that briefing congressional committees constitutes "participation" because it involves communication with an external body. However, the definition explicitly states that Congress, its committees, and its members are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, reporting to or briefing Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
